full_judgment: 3. When the Money Execution case was proceeding the petitioner Bazlul Ghani filed an objection petition under Order 21 rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure against attachment of the property in question in the said Money Execution Case No. 11 of 1969 alleging that the property attached in Money Execution Case belongs to Bazlul Gani being Settlement Plot No. 721 covering an area of 0.13 decimals of land at Kandipar, Comilla on which stands a 2-storied pucca building and other katcha structures which originally belonged to Pulin Behari Gupta in SA Plot Nos. 814, 815 and 816 covering an area of 0.11 decimals of land with some structures and it now stands in the name of the petitioner Bazlul Ghani and he is never a judgment-debtor. It has been alleged that Pulin Bchari Gupta and Binod Behari Gupta, the two brothers, were owners in possession of the property in question by succession from their father late Umesh Chandra Gupta. The said two brothers sold the property in question to Girish Chandra Sen by a registered kabala dated 12th March, 1926 and delivered physical possession wherein Girish Chandra Sen lived for more than 12 years. After his death his other properties including the property in question devolved upon his two sons namely, Promod Kumar Sen and Kumud Kanti Sen and by amicable partition the property in question fell in the saham of Kumud Kanti Sen. The said Kumud Kanti Sen sold the property by a registered kabala dated 9.1.1956 to Madhabendra Roy Chowdhury, Pranabendra Roy Chowdhury and Kcshobendra Roy Chowdhury, sons of Srecjut Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury. The real purchaser was however Srcejut Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury and his sons were benamders. Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury remained in possession as purchaser and thereafter Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury corrected the khatian beine, Khatian No. 389 of the schedule property in his name and paid taxes and municipal rent regularly in his name. Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury executed a will in favour of his son Kcshobendra Roy Chowdhury on 28.10.1969 in respect of some immovable property including the present property in question. Monindra Chandra Roy Chowdhury was killed by the Pakistani Army during the Liberation period of 1971 and thereupon his son Keshobendra Chandra Roy Chowdhury brought Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1972 in the court of District Judge, Comilla and obtained a probate of the said will thereby acquiring all the rights in the schedule property. The said Keshobendra Roy Chowdhury while in exclusive owner ship sold the same with easement right to the petitioner Bazlul Ghani by a kabala dated 14.1.1974 and delivered possession and the petitioner is in peaceful uninterrupted possession of the same. The petitioner affected separation of the holding leading to Zama Khariz. Khatian No. 212 was opened in his name on the strength of possession, title deed as well as by adverse possession vides Separation Case No. 13/73-74 in the office of the Sadar Circle Officer Revenue, Comilla and his name is also recorded in the Municipal record. It has been the case of the petitioner that the Judgment-debtor Hiramoya Prova never owned and possessed the schedule property and she is a stranger to the suit property without any legal right. There is no basis for putting the schedule property to auction. It has been claimed that the schedule property was never actually mortgaged with the bank and the officials of the opposite party fraudulently, collusively included in the 5th schedule of the Money Execution Case the property as mortgaged property subjecting it to attachment.
